items.text: The page titles differ. A uses a generic descriptive title. B's title pairs the brand name with the hero headline.
items.evidence: A title: "Payment Processing & Merchant Services"; B title: "Merchant Savvy – Payment Processing Made Simple (& Cheaper)"

items.text: A's h1 element is empty. B's h1 has a visible headline.
items.evidence: A h1.text = ""; B h1.text = "Payment Processing Made Simple (& Cheaper)"

items.text: Both pages share the same three h2 section names, in the same order.
items.evidence: Both heading_outlines list h2 "Payment Processing", "Finance & Banking", "Research & Stats"

items.text: B uses semantic header, main and footer landmarks. A has none of these and relies on section and nav elements.
items.evidence: semantic: A header=0, main=0, footer=0, section=15, nav=4; B header=1, main=1, footer=1, section=3, nav=1

items.text: A uses several web fonts: Open Sans, Roboto, Calibri, Font Awesome and eicons. B uses only the system-ui font stack.
items.evidence: A fonts: Open Sans 534, roboto 438, Roboto 140, calibri 134, Font Awesome 5 Free 18, eicons 2; B fonts: system-ui 112

items.text: B's h1 is larger, bolder, white and centred. A's h1 is 38px, semibold, dark navy and left-aligned (but empty).
items.evidence: A h1: 38px, weight 600, rgb(0,37,58), align start; B h1: 54.4px, weight 700, rgb(255,255,255), align center

items.text: A's links use a bright cyan-blue color. B's link text is dark on white cards, with indigo arrows and labels.
items.evidence: A top_text_colors includes rgb(19,175,240) ×154 (cyan links in slice 01); B text colors include rgb(30,34,140) ×11

items.text: B is built around a deep indigo and amber palette. A's computed backgrounds include green, purple, orange-red and light blue-grey, but its visible render is mostly white.
A's logo image is very small (48×11). B's header logo is 157×36.
items.evidence: A merchant_savvy_purple.svg rect w48 h11 at y24; B same file rect w157 h36

items.text: B's hero has a row of four translucent cards, each with an amber circular check icon and a value-proposition line.
items.evidence: B_slice_00: cards reading "We'll get you preferential rates…", "Access 90% of the UK's leading acquiring banks", etc.; backgrounds rgba(255,

items.text: B has a visible top navigation bar: logo on the left, text links (Merchant Accounts, Card Machines, Online, EPOS) and a pill-shaped "Quotes" link in indigo.
items.evidence: B_slice_00 header; B border_radius bucket_pill=2

items.text: B places a white rounded panel of payment logos (Visa, Mastercard, Google Pay, Apple Pay, contactless) in the hero.
items.evidence: B msuk-payment-logos image 300×50 at y604, alt "Accepted payment card logos"

items.text: B has more visible copy than A.
items.evidence: text_stats words: A 131, B 192

items.text: B uses emoji as image placeholders in its research cards (phone, shopping cart, laptop).
items.evidence: emoji count B=4 vs A=1; B_slice_01 cards show 📱, 🛒, 💻 on indigo gradients

items.text: B stacks each section vertically (heading, then description, then a grid of bordered link cards with arrow icons).
items.evidence: B_slice_00/01: Payment Processing in a 4-column grid of 8 cards; Finance & Banking in a 3-column grid of 6 cards; display_grid=7

items.text: A uses no CSS grid and lots of flex. B mixes grid with a small number of flex containers.
items.evidence: layout: A display_grid 0, display_flex 179; B display_grid 7, display_flex 18

items.text: B separates sections with alternating background bands: white, then pale lavender for Finance & Banking, then white again.
items.evidence: B bg rgb(243,243,250) on the Finance & Banking band in B_slice_00/01; A sections are all white

items.text: B shows the five research items as uniform rounded cards in a 3-column grid, with a bold indigo "Title →" label under each image.
items.evidence: B_slice_01: UK SMEs, Mobile Payments, Mobile Ecommerce, Remote Working, Payment Fraud cards; image_overlaps empty; charts.jpg rendered at 34

items.text: A renders research thumbnails at 208×139 with plain grey captions. B renders them larger, at 347×232.
items.evidence: charts.jpg rect: A w208 h139; B w347 h232; same for payment-fraud-stats.jpg

items.text: A's alt text is auto-generated from filenames with a "Homepage (New Design)" prefix. B uses short descriptive alts, or empty alts for decorative thumbnails.
items.evidence: A alt e.g. "Homepage (New Design) merchant savvy purple"; B alt "Merchant Savvy", "Accepted payment card logos", "" for charts.jpg

items.text: A's footer is plain grey text on white with cyan Privacy/Terms links. B's footer is a dark navy band with a white logo, white text and underlined links on the right.
items.evidence: A_slice_02: grey copyright lines, cyan links; B_slice_01/02: rgb(20,22,94) footer, white logo, underlined "Privacy Policy" and "Terms Of Use

items.text: B repeats the logo in the footer. A shows the logo only once.
items.evidence: B merchant_savvy_purple.svg appears twice (y16 and y2443); A once (y24)

items.text: A uses mostly square corners, with only a few rounded elements. B has many 8–15px radii and pill shapes.
B uses gradient backgrounds in the hero and the placeholder research cards.
items.evidence: gradient_backgrounds A 2, B 4; B_slice_00 hero indigo gradient, B_slice_01 gradient card images

items.text: The pages were captured at different widths and heights.
items.evidence: page_width/height: A 1868×2877, B 1440×2688

items.text: A uses Font Awesome chevron icons for its link lists. B uses arrow (→) icons inside its link cards and after its card titles.
items.evidence: A fonts include Font Awesome 5 Free (18 elements), chevrons in A_slice_01; B_slice_00/01 show → arrows in each card

items.text: Both pages declare British English.
items.evidence: lang: A en-GB, B en-GB

items.text: A's DOM is very large and nested. B's is small and flat.
items.evidence: A: 405 divs, 227 li, 188 spans, 105 anchors, 174 inputs, 3 forms, 3 iframes, 95 scripts. B: 18 divs, 25 li, 8 spans, 35 anchors, 1 script, n

items.text: A relies on external stylesheets and heavy inline styling. B uses a single embedded style block with no inline styles.
items.evidence: A: stylesheets 44, style tags 9, inline_style_attrs 304, link 62. B: stylesheets 0, style 1, inline_style_attrs 0.

items.text: A's class usage is verbose and builder-generated. B uses very few classes.
items.evidence: A classes: total 2572, unique 416. B classes: total 39, unique 21. Tailwind-like fraction is about 0 on both.

items.text: A's content is left-heavy and leaves the right third empty. B's content is centered in a max-width container.
items.evidence: A page_width 1868, with links ending near x≈1200 and the images row ending at about x≈1450. B page_width 1440, with content spanning x=180–1

items.text: A has far more transitions and some transforms, which suggests a script-driven UI. B has few transitions and no transforms.
items.evidence: A transitions 377, transforms 6. B transitions 19, transforms 0. Neither has animations (both 0).

items.text: A footer copy runs on tight line-height with the lines almost touching. B spaces its lines out and sets them in white.
items.evidence: A_slice_02 shows 3 compact lines of 'Copyright © ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 2021 ...'. B_slice_01 shows 3 separated lines at about 27px pitch.

features.statement: Page title pairs the brand name with the hero headline, using a dash separator.
Hero contains a visible, centered, large bold white h1 headline.
Uses semantic header, main and footer landmarks with few section and nav elements.
Typography relies solely on the system-ui font stack, with no web fonts.
Palette is built on deep indigo with amber accents and pale lavender surfaces.
Header logo is rendered prominently at a larger size.
Hero shows a row of translucent cards, each with a circular amber check icon and a value-proposition line.
Top navigation bar has logo at left, text links, and a pill-shaped indigo call-to-action link.
A white rounded panel of payment-method logos sits in the hero as a trust cue.
Emoji are used as icon-like placeholders in image cards on gradient backgrounds.
Sections stack vertically: heading, description, then a grid of uniform bordered link cards with arrow icons.
Layout mixes CSS grid for card sections with a few flex containers.
Sections are separated by alternating background bands of white and pale tint.
Card thumbnails render large with consistent sizes and short descriptive or empty decorative alt text.
Card titles use bold indigo labels followed by an arrow glyph (→).
Footer is a dark navy band with repeated white logo, white text and underlined links.
Corners are generously rounded, with 8–15px radii on cards and pill shapes on buttons.
Hero and card imagery use gradient backgrounds.
Content is centered within a max-width container.
DOM is small and flat with few classes, a single embedded style block and no inline styles.
Motion is minimal, with few transitions and no transforms.
